items.stem: What is a Vendor Rep in SDM?

options.text: A representative of a 3rd-party supplier that SDM creates and maintains because HR doesn't manage them
A school-board trustee seat imported from HRAD
A CSSD staff member with a temporary job under six weeks
An AAD security group that grants editing rights over an area

items.explanation: Vendor Reps are representatives of 3rd-party suppliers. They're one of the staffing categories HR doesn't manage, so SDM creates and maintains them directly.

misconceptions.b: That describes Trustee Positions, not Vendor Reps.
misconceptions.c: Temporary jobs are HR-gap staffing on the Staff side, not vendor representatives.
misconceptions.d: That describes Data Owners, an access construct — not a vendor representative.

items.stem: What does SDM provision for a Vendor Rep?

options.text: A login account and a matching CSSD email, but no other access to CSSD assets
Full access to CSSD systems, files, and sites
Only a row in DDH with no account or email
A school assignment and District Program links

items.explanation: A Vendor Rep gets a login account and a matching CSSD email — and deliberately nothing more; no other access to CSSD assets.

misconceptions.b: The access is narrow by design — a login and CSSD email only, not broad system access.
misconceptions.c: They do get an account and a CSSD email; it isn't a data-only record.
misconceptions.d: Schools and District Program links belong to the Schools page, not to a Vendor Rep.

items.stem: Why does SDM maintain Vendor Reps directly instead of receiving them from a system of record?

options.text: Because vendors are one of the staffing categories HR doesn't manage
Because HRAD exports vendors but the sync is disabled in dev
Because Vendor Reps are created and deleted only in SharePoint
Because the AuditLog generates vendor records automatically

items.explanation: Vendors are an HR-gap category — HR doesn't manage them — so SDM creates and maintains them itself rather than importing them.

misconceptions.b: There is no HRAD vendor feed; vendors are an HR gap SDM fills directly.
misconceptions.c: Vendor Reps are created and maintained in SDM, not in SharePoint.
misconceptions.d: The AuditLog records changes; it doesn't generate vendor records.

items.stem: A 3rd-party supplier sends a technician who needs to sign in and be reachable on a CSSD address for one engagement. How should this be handled?

options.text: Create a Vendor Rep in SDM, which provisions a login account and matching CSSD email and nothing more
Wait for HR to onboard the technician through the HR system of record
Grant the technician the same access a CSSD staff member receives
Add the technician as a contractor on the Staff page

items.explanation: This is exactly the Vendor Rep case: a 3rd-party supplier's representative gets a login and a matching CSSD email, with no other access to CSSD assets.

misconceptions.b: HR doesn't manage vendors — that's why SDM owns them; waiting on HR means the rep never gets provisioned.
misconceptions.c: A Vendor Rep is an external supplier, not staff; granting staff-level access over-provisions them.
misconceptions.d: Contractors are HR-gap staffing (S3.5); a supplier's representative is a Vendor Rep, a distinct category.

items.stem: Both Vendor Reps and contractors are HR-gap categories SDM owns. What distinguishes a Vendor Rep from a contractor?

options.text: A Vendor Rep represents a 3rd-party supplier and is provisioned with only a login and CSSD email; a contractor is HR-gap staffing on the Staff side
A Vendor Rep comes from HRAD while a contractor is created in SDM
There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
A contractor gets no account, while a Vendor Rep gets full CSSD access

items.explanation: Both fill an HR gap, but they're distinct: a contractor (which also covers student teachers and volunteers) is HR-gap staffing handled on the Staff side, while a Vendor Rep represents a 3rd-party supplier and gets only a login and a matching CSSD email.

misconceptions.b: Both are created in SDM precisely because HR doesn't manage them; neither comes from HRAD.
misconceptions.c: They are distinct categories — a supplier's representative is not a contractor.
misconceptions.d: A Vendor Rep's access is narrow (login + CSSD email, no other access), not full CSSD access.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain why SDM owns Vendor Reps and what access a Vendor Rep is given.
rubric: States Vendor Reps are representatives of 3rd-party suppliers that SDM creates/maintains because HR doesn't manage them
States the access scope: a login account and a matching CSSD email, with no other access to CSSD assets
items.sampleAnswer: Vendor Reps are representatives of 3rd-party suppliers, and since HR doesn't manage them SDM creates and maintains them itself. Each rep gets a login account and a matching CSSD email, but no other access to CSSD assets.
